seoDescription: Hit by a semi or delivery truck in Troy, Michigan? 2,081 heavy trucks and buses were involved in Oakland County crashes in 2024. tagline: I-75 carries freight through the middle of Troy, and the industrial corridors along Stephenson Highway, Maple, and the east side ship and receive it all day. When one of those trucks causes a crash, the carrier, the trailer’s owner, and sometimes the shipper are part of the case.

c.v: I-75 runs through the middle of Troy, carrying freight between Detroit, the Auburn Hills and Pontiac automotive corridor, Flint, and points north, with interchanges at Fourteen Mile, Rochester, Big Beaver, and Crooks (exits 65 to 72) that feed directly into the city’s industrial areas. Along Stephenson Highway beside the freeway, and in the industrial and office parks along Maple Road, Coolidge, John R, and Dequindre, manufacturers, suppliers, distributors, and service companies receive and ship freight by tractor-trailer and box truck every day. Car haulers serve the dealerships of the Troy Motor Mall, and delivery trucks serve Somerset, Oakland Mall, the Rochester Road retail, and the Big Beaver office towers. In 2024, according to the Michigan State Police, 2,081 heavy trucks and buses were involved in crashes in Oakland County, and 110 people were killed and 3,613 injured in heavy truck and bus crashes statewide.

A truck crash is not a car crash with a larger vehicle. The driver and the carrier are governed by federal safety regulations whose violation is evidence of negligence. The carrier must hold $750,000 or more in insurance. The records that prove the case, the driver’s electronic logs and the truck’s engine data, can be lawfully discarded within months, and the carrier’s insurer will have an investigator on the case within days. I-75 through the city.

I-75 through Troy was rebuilt and widened in the I-75 modernization project. Its truck crashes are rear-end and underride crashes in the stop-and-go at the Big Beaver and Crooks interchanges during the office commute; lane changes into a car in the blind spot on the right side of the cab; merge crashes where trucks enter from the industrial corridors; and rollovers and jackknifes on the ramps when a truck takes them too fast or its load shifts (49 CFR Part 393). Traffic coming north from the I-75/I-696 interchange in Royal Oak and Madison Heights arrives already weaving for the Troy exits.
Stephenson Highway and the industrial corridors.

Stephenson Highway runs beside I-75 through the city’s industrial area, and the Maple Road, Coolidge, John R, and Dequindre corridors hold more industrial and flex buildings. Tractor-trailers and box trucks turn wide into loading docks and driveways across two lanes; back into docks from the road; stop in a travel lane waiting to enter; and pull out into fast traffic with limited sight lines. When a facility’s dock layout, traffic control, or delivery schedule puts trucks in the road, the facility or its logistics provider may share responsibility with the carrier.
Car haulers and the dealerships.

The Troy Motor Mall’s dealerships receive vehicles by car-hauler, often unloaded on or beside the road. A car-hauler blocking a lane, a vehicle rolling off a ramp, and a hauler pulling out across traffic are the cases; the dealership, the hauler, and the shipper may each have a role.
Big Beaver, Rochester Road, and the retail.

Delivery trucks serving Somerset, Oakland Mall, the Rochester Road strips, the office towers, and the hotels and restaurants: wide right turns, trucks backing into service drives, trucks double-parked or stopped in a lane, and crashes with pedestrians at the malls and the restaurant row (see our
pedestrian accident page
Whose road it is.

I-75 is MDOT’s; a road-defect claim against the State goes to the Court of Claims, with written notice filed there within 120 days (MCL 691.1404). The Road Commission for Oakland County has jurisdiction over many of Troy’s major roads and operates the city’s traffic signals, and the City maintains its local streets and its own major streets; a claim against the City or the Road Commission takes written notice within 120 days (MCL 691.1404).

sections.heading: Who is responsible, and who pays

c.v: The carrier, not just the driver.

The motor carrier is responsible for its drivers’ compliance with the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Regulations and is liable for a driver’s negligence in the course of employment. Michigan applies the federal rules to intrastate carriers (MCL 480.11a), so a local hauler running between Troy suppliers and the Auburn Hills plants is held to the same standards as an interstate carrier. The rules that decide truck cases most often:

c.v: The owner of the truck or trailer.

In Michigan, a vehicle’s owner is liable for its negligent operation by someone driving with the owner’s consent (MCL 257.401). When the tractor, the trailer, and the driver belong to different companies, which is common in freight, each may be a defendant, although a company in the business of renting or leasing vehicles is generally shielded from owner liability by federal law (49 USC 30106).
Michigan no-fault still applies to you.

Your own auto insurer pays your medical bills, 85 percent of lost wages up to the monthly cap DIFS sets each year, replacement services, and attendant care regardless of fault (MCL 500.3107), with written notice due within one year (MCL 500.3145(1)). The Michigan Assigned Claims Plan pays if no household policy applies (MCL 500.3172). Your claim against the driver and the carrier for pain and suffering and losses beyond no-fault requires a threshold injury (MCL 500.3135) and must be filed within three years (MCL 600.5805(2)). That claim includes wage loss above the no-fault cap or beyond three years (MCL 500.3135(3)(c)), which for many Troy professionals is a large part of the loss. If you were more than 50 percent at fault, you cannot recover pain-and-suffering damages, and below that your share reduces them (MCL 500.3135(2)(b)). The difference from a car case is the money available: the carrier’s $750,000-plus policy, often with excess coverage above it. See our
no-fault insurance claim page
Other defendants.

The shipper or broker that loaded the trailer or hired an unsafe carrier; the facility or logistics provider whose dock operations contributed; the dealership whose unloading practice put a car-hauler in the road; the maintenance contractor; the manufacturer of a failed component (
product liability
); and, for a government truck (City of Troy, the Road Commission, MDOT, SMART), the agency under the motor vehicle exception to governmental immunity (MCL 691.1405).
If you were the truck driver.

Workers’ compensation pays your benefits, and your employer usually cannot be sued (MCL 418.131). If you were injured in your employer’s truck, no-fault benefits generally come from the insurer of that truck (MCL 500.3114(3)), coordinated with comp, which is paid first (MCL 500.3109(1)). You can also sue a third party, such as another driver or a facility whose dock operation caused the crash. See our
workers’ compensation page

sections.heading: The evidence, and how fast it disappears

c.v: Carriers must keep hours-of-service records for six months (49 CFR 395.8) and driver inspection reports for three months (49 CFR 396.11); after that the regulations no longer require them. MDOT freeway cameras on I-75, business, dealership, and office cameras along Stephenson, Maple, and Big Beaver, and dash cameras overwrite in days to weeks. The truck’s engine control module and event data recorder can be cleared when it is repaired and returned to service.
The first act in a Troy truck case is a
preservation letter

: to the carrier, its insurer, the tractor and trailer owners, the shipper or broker, and, where the crash happened at or near a facility or dealership, that business and its logistics provider. It demands the ELD and engine data, dash camera footage, the driver’s qualification file and post-crash test results, dispatch records and bills of lading, dock appointment and arrival logs, maintenance files, and the truck itself for inspection. Once a party knows a claim is coming, destroying that evidence exposes it to spoliation sanctions.

faqs.question: How many truck accidents happen in Troy?

answer.v: The State does not publish truck crash figures by city. Countywide, 2,081 heavy trucks and buses were involved in Oakland County crashes in 2024, and statewide 15,888 crashes involved a heavy truck or bus.

faqs.question: I was rear-ended by a semi on I-75 at Big Beaver. Who pays?

answer.v: Your own no-fault insurer pays your medical bills and lost wages first, regardless of fault. The carrier’s insurer pays for pain and suffering and losses beyond no-fault, including wages above the no-fault cap, once a threshold injury is established. In a rear-end crash, fault is rarely the dispute; the truck’s speed, the driver’s hours, and the following distance in the engine data decide how strong the claim is.

faqs.question: A truck was stopped in the lane on Maple waiting to get into a dock, and I hit it. Is that my fault?

answer.v: Not necessarily. Following too closely is usually the claim against the rear driver, but a truck stopped in a travel lane without warning, or a facility whose dock schedule routinely stacks trucks in the road, can carry fault too. The dock logs, the cameras, and the truck’s data decide it.

faqs.question: A car-hauler was unloading on the road outside a dealership. Who is responsible?

answer.v: Possibly the hauler, the carrier, and the dealership, depending on who chose where and how the vehicles were unloaded. Photograph the scene, including where the hauler was parked.

faqs.question: I drive a truck for a Troy company and was hurt in a crash. What are my claims?

answer.v: Workers’ compensation through your employer, no-fault benefits coordinated with comp, and a lawsuit against any third party who caused the crash.

faqs.question: Why does the lawyer need to act within days?

answer.v: Because the records expire: six months for hours-of-service logs, three months for inspection reports, days or weeks for camera footage, and the truck’s electronic data can be cleared on repair.

faqs.question: Is a truck case worth more than a car case?

answer.v: The injuries are usually worse and the insurance is usually larger: a $750,000 minimum for a general freight carrier, against $50,000 for a minimally insured car.
